label: July–December 1881
atlas_dek: The episodes reported from July through December 1881 in our dossiers: lynchings of any race and anti-Black violence, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some events were first reported the month after). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 255 episodes reported from July through December 1881. These months cover two things: lynchings and attempted or threatened lynchings of any race, and anti-Black violence or threats more broadly. Lynchings of white, Mexican, Italian and Chinese victims, and lynchings where no report gives the victim’s race, are therefore included here, unlike in our other months. The episodes come from the located events in each month’s table, which include events from the month before that were first reported later; from the Monroe Work Today inventory, our only lynching list for this year; and, for July and August, from a check of every article for attacks by one person. Each month’s search also read the following month’s papers for more on known episodes, and December’s read January 1882. For 1881 the search used white papers only.

We wrote 300 dossiers; 45 are set aside, and 11 more events got no dossier because the table alone showed them out of scope. Set aside: five legal executions misreported as violence (among them Henry Lawson at Chattanooga, the man a July mob had tried to lynch); four duplicates; four events from other months; anti-Black-scope events in which no report gives anyone’s race and no lynching was involved (twenty); events with no force, two-sided fights, a bystander killed by a stray bullet in a north Georgia circus riot, reports a contemporary source denied, and a joke item from Tombstone.

Inventory differences are kept and noted, not counted: the ambush of Mexican traders at Las Animas (Monroe Work Today lists thirteen victims near Fronteras; the papers place a robbery ambush in Sonora), and Perry Thompson in Sharkey County, Mississippi, whom the inventory lists as lynched and the papers describe as killed when hidden men fired on Black men walking to a political meeting.

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing or resisting arrest are included, and only gunfights over an arrest or a crime in progress are set aside from the totals. Two-sided fights and threats with no force stay in the reader but out of the totals. Peonage, force used to hold a Black worker to labor, is always included.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched the papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. White-press clippings are page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
